$comment: Product-track listings: finished Catholic software people use, as opposed to
the developer building blocks in seed.json.
Regenerate with: node scripts/build-seed.mjs data/products.json migrations/0004_products.sql
`launched_at` is deliberately null throughout. We know roughly when most of
these appeared but not precisely, and a launch feed built on invented dates
is worse than one built on when a listing joined the directory. Submitters
state their own launch date; ours stay blank until someone confirms one.
Pricing here describes the shape of the offer, not a specific figure, because
figures go stale and a wrong price is worse than no price.

listings.name: Hallow
listings.tagline: The prayer and meditation app that took Catholic devotion mainstream.
listings.description: Guided rosaries, examens, lectio divina, night prayer and sleep-time scripture, with reading plans and community challenges around Lent and Advent. The production values are the point: audio is properly produced and the onboarding assumes you might be coming back to prayer after years away. A free tier covers a daily selection; the subscription unlocks the full library.
listings.pricing_note: Free daily selection; subscription for the full library.

listings.name: Universalis
listings.tagline: The Liturgy of the Hours and daily Mass, done properly and offline.
listings.description: Every hour of the Divine Office plus the readings for Mass, calculated for your calendar and available without a connection. Unfashionable interface, unimpeachable substance — it handles the propers, the ranks and the regional calendars that prettier apps quietly skip. A long-standing favourite of clergy and religious for exactly that reason.
listings.pricing_note: Free on the web; one-time purchase for the apps and ebooks.

listings.name: iBreviary
listings.tagline: The breviary and missal in your pocket, free, in several languages.
listings.description: One of the first serious Catholic apps and still going: the full Liturgy of the Hours and the Roman Missal, in Italian, English, Spanish, French, Portuguese and Latin, including the extraordinary form. Free with no tier above it.

listings.name: Divine Office
listings.tagline: The Hours prayed aloud, with a community reciting alongside you.
listings.description: Audio recordings of every hour of the breviary, recorded with a small group so the psalms are prayed antiphonally rather than read at you. Podcast, apps and web. Useful if you find the office easier to keep by ear than by page. The same apostolate publishes the JSON feeds listed on the API side of this directory.
listings.pricing_note: Free podcast and web; paid apps support the apostolate.

listings.name: Magnificat
listings.tagline: The monthly worship aid, in print and on a screen.
listings.description: Daily Mass texts, morning and evening prayer, and a curated meditation for each day, published monthly. The editorial selection is the value — someone has chosen the readings and the art for you. Print subscription with digital access.

listings.name: Ascension
listings.tagline: Bible in a Year, Catechism in a Year, and the study programmes behind them.
listings.description: The publisher whose podcasts pulled hundreds of thousands of people through the whole Bible and the whole Catechism a chapter a day. The podcasts are free; the study programmes, the Great Adventure Bible and the parish materials are what you pay for. Their reading-plan structure is the thing most imitators get wrong and they get right.
listings.pricing_note: Podcasts free; books, courses and parish programmes paid.

listings.name: FORMED
listings.tagline: Catholic streaming — films, studies and audio — usually free through your parish.
listings.description: The Augustine Institute's streaming service: documentaries, sacramental prep, children's programming and audio talks. Most people get access free because their parish subscribes, which makes it the default answer when a DRE asks where to find video for a class. Individual subscriptions exist too.
listings.pricing_note: Parish subscriptions give parishioners free access; individual plans available.

listings.name: Word on Fire
listings.tagline: Bishop Barron's evangelisation ministry: video, essays and the Bible commentaries.
listings.description: Sermons, the CATHOLICISM series, daily gospel reflections by email, and a growing shelf of published Bibles and commentaries. Much of the video and writing is free; the institute membership and the print editions are paid. Aimed squarely at the seeker and the lapsed rather than the already-convinced.
listings.pricing_note: Most video and writing free; membership and books paid.

listings.name: Exodus 90
listings.tagline: A ninety-day ascetic programme for men, with a fraternity to keep you honest.
listings.description: Cold showers, no alcohol, no screens for entertainment, an hour of prayer, and a small group that notices when you stop. Structured as a daily plan tied to readings from Exodus. Demanding by design and unusually specific about what it asks — which is why it works for the people it works for.

listings.name: Catholic Answers
listings.tagline: Apologetics: the searchable archive of answers to the hard questions.
listings.description: Decades of tracts, articles, radio archives and forum answers on doctrine, scripture and the objections people actually raise. Free and enormous. The first place to look when you need a sourced answer rather than an opinion, and a useful corpus if you are building anything that needs to cite.

listings.name: Magisterium AI
listings.tagline: Ask the Church a question and get an answer with the citations attached.
listings.description: The consumer side of the engine whose API is listed on the developer track: put a question in plain language, get an answer drawn from councils, encyclicals, the Catechism and canon law, with references you can follow. The citations are the feature — you can check it, which is more than most AI assistants let you do. Free tier with a prompt limit, subscription above it.
listings.pricing_note: Free prompt allowance; subscription for unlimited use.

listings.name: The Pillar
listings.tagline: Catholic journalism that reports on the institution rather than for it.
listings.description: News and analysis on the Church as a governed body — finances, canon law, appointments, the things that get covered thinly elsewhere. Free newsletter with paid subscriber posts. Read it for the canonical detail; the reporters know the code and it shows.
listings.pricing_note: Free posts; paid subscription for the full archive.

listings.name: Vatican News
listings.tagline: The Holy See's own newsroom, in dozens of languages.
listings.description: Official coverage of the pope and the Roman curia from the Dicastery for Communication, published in a long list of languages with audio from Vatican Radio. The primary source when you need what was actually said rather than what was reported.

listings.name: eCatholic
listings.tagline: Parish websites for staff who are not web developers.
listings.description: Hosted websites, giving and communication tools built for parishes and dioceses, with templates that already know what a Mass schedule and a bulletin are. The realistic alternative to a volunteer maintaining WordPress, which is the situation it is actually competing against.

listings.name: Laudate
listings.tagline: The Swiss army knife Catholic app, free since before that was normal.
listings.description: Readings, the rosary, the Divine Mercy chaplet, the Liturgy of the Hours, the Catechism, prayers, a confession examen and more, crammed into one free app with no subscription. The interface shows its age; the coverage is still hard to beat for the price, which is nothing.

listings.name: Catholic Digital Commons
listings.tagline: Open infrastructure for Catholic builders, including a Bible API.
listings.description: A project putting shared Catholic digital resources in the commons rather than behind fifteen separate paywalls — among them a Bible API. Sits exactly on the seam between this directory's two tracks: an organisation to know about, and a source of the building blocks listed on the developer side.

listings.name: Latinitas: Learn Latin
listings.tagline: Church Latin taught through the prayers you already know.
listings.description: Teaches Latin in situ rather than as isolated vocabulary: you meet the genitive in the Sign of the Cross and the subjunctive in the petitions of the Our Father. Fifteen foundational prayers across four modules — Prayers of the Faith, Devotional Prayers, the Rosary and Sacred Liturgy — with translation, fill-the-blank, build-the-verse and grammar exercises, plus history and context for each text. Gamified with XP, streaks and ranks from Catechumen to Magister.

listings.name: Woly: Christian Goodnight
listings.tagline: Personalised bedtime stories built around the virtues.
listings.description: Generates a short, age-appropriate bedtime story around a child's name, age and a chosen virtue — faith, hope, charity, justice, prudence, temperance or fortitude — in under a minute, with recorded narration and optional ambient sound. Aimed at families who want the last thing said at night to be formative rather than incidental. Favourites can be saved and re-read.

listings.name: 30-30-30 V
listings.tagline: The 30-30-30 morning routine, with a virtue attached to each day.
listings.description: Tracks the routine the name describes — 30g of protein within 30 minutes of waking, then 30 minutes of low-intensity movement — with streaks, XP and check-off from an Apple Watch. The faith framing is real but light-touch: a Daily Virtue accompanies each morning, and the stated rationale is stewardship of the body as temple rather than fitness for its own sake. If you want prayer or study, look elsewhere in the directory; if you want a habit tracker that does not leave your faith at the door, this is it.

listings.name: Hearthly
listings.tagline: One household task at a time, for people who stall at a list.
listings.description: Serves a single cleaning task chosen for you rather than a backlog, in five- to fifteen-minute pieces, built explicitly for ADHD minds and anyone whom a full list simply defeats. Finished tasks water a virtual garden. The faith content is one thread rather than a feature set: Proverbs 31:27 anchors the whole thing — keeping a household as quiet work worth doing well. Not a devotional, but a home-care app that is clear about why it thinks the work matters.
